newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end at record levels in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end at record levels in quiet trading.

text.p: Swiss shares ended at a record close on Monday after a day of quiet trade that was characterised by position-squaring and window dressing ahead of the year-end.
Trading on Tuesday is expected to be even quieter -- if possible -- and the Swiss Exchange will close early at 1300 GMT.
The blue-chip SMI index closed 26.1 points higher at a record 3,948.3. There was an intraday record high of 3,951.3.
The broad SPI ended 14.38 points higher at 2,515.46, also a record close.
Drug stocks led the active list with Roche up 60 Swiss francs to 10,495 and Novartis up 19 to 1,528.
Among banks, UBS bearers were seven francs lower at 1,169 with dealers saying a Zurich-based bank was swapping UBS for shares of Swiss Bank Corp (SBC).
SBC registered shares rose four francs to 255.75 francs. But trading volume in SBC was much lower than in UBS.

Dealers said the weak Swiss franc, which usually supports the shares of export-companies, was ignored but it should help drive shares higher in the first days of 1997 when investors will return to the market.
